Number of earlier check-ins that form the personal baseline for anomaly scoring.
Fewer baseline check-ins than this means no anomaly score is given.

Smallest allowed standard deviation, as a fraction of the baseline mean, so tiny spreads do not inflate z-scores. 0.05 keeps ordinary day-to-day changes (a few mmHg or bpm) from looking unusual against the very steady simulated history.
z-score that gives an anomaly score of 0.5 (anomaly score = max |z| / (2 x z_alert)).

Projected loss at or above this percentage gives an alert status for a bone site.
Projected loss at or above this percentage gives a watch status for a bone site.
Reference shielding at which the mission background dose rate applies.
Shielding thickness over which the galactic cosmic ray background falls by a factor of e. Set so that 20 g/cm2 removes about 25% of the dose, the most that added shielding gives (exp(-20/70) = 0.75).
Unshielded dose rate of a severity 1 particle event before mission factors: an August 1972 class event gives about 50 mSv/h behind 5 g/cm2, so 50 x exp(5/8) = 93 mSv/h unshielded.
Shielding thickness over which particle event dose falls by a factor of e.
Length of a particle event with no end time.
Career radiation limit used for the percent-of-limit figure.
